name: Solomon's Plea to Westfall
summary: In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon calls on Westfall for help as Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten Redridge. Stormwind's royal army has not answered, so he asks Gryan Stoutmantle to send the People's Militia.

sections.title: A Desperate Call for Aid
sections.body: Blackrock orcs and hostile gnolls threaten Redridge, while Magistrate Solomon is isolated in Lakeshire. Stormwind's royal army has not arrived in force to defend the region's borders. With no time to wait for the capital, Solomon writes beyond the regular army. Word has reached him of a volunteer defense force forming in Elwynn to the west, so he appeals to the People's Militia.

sections.title: Reaching Across the Border
sections.body: Solomon addresses his message to Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran warrior organizing Westfall's frontier defense. He hopes Stoutmantle can spare fighters for Lakeshire until Stormwind sends regular reserves. An adventurer carries the document. Stormwind's outlying territories are poorly coordinated, so local magistrates must arrange mutual aid on their own.

faq.q: What is Solomon's Plea to Westfall?
faq.answer: Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire writes to Gryan Stoutmantle and asks the People's Militia in Westfall to send reinforcements for Redridge's defense.

faq.q: Why is Magistrate Solomon asking Westfall for help instead of Stormwind?
faq.answer: Stormwind's royal troops have not arrived in force as danger grows in Lakeshire. With no time to wait for the Crown, Solomon seeks help from a nearby fighting force.
Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People's Militia, a volunteer defense league of local farmers and settlers protecting Westfall from the Defias Brotherhood.

faq.q: What threats are pushing Solomon to send this letter?
faq.answer: Blackrock orcs are invading, and gnolls raid throughout the Redridge Mountains. Their attacks strain Lakeshire's town guard.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Solomon's appeal shows outlying towns turning to local volunteers when royal troops do not arrive.
As a human, you can see how strained rural settlements have become. The missing king and political neglect leave frontier lands vulnerable.
